symptom: mendixlabs/mxcli#1517 (ako#1399): three scope verdicts of one `alter microflow` block disagreed with the flow the block writes. (A2) a consistent rename — producer, log and return replaced in one block — was refused by check and exec: "replace $Code = call microflow …: $Code is still used by: log …; return $Code". (B2) `insert after X begin declare $Late … end; replace log … with begin …$Late… end;` was refused MDL090 "the fragment uses $Late, which is not declared on the path". (B3) `replace loop` whose body read an undefined $Nope passed check, exec said "Altered microflow", and mx check (11.6.6 and 11.15.0 alike) gave CE0109 "Undefined variable 'Nope'"
cause: applyTo ran checkOutputUnused per operation, in order, against the stored candidates, so readers a later operation replaces still counted, and an in-place return/condition edit never retired its stored reads; checkFragmentScope consulted own/inScope/removedByOps but not what earlier operations declared (unscopedRefs did, but unconditionally, without position); and it read a fragment's variables from formatActivity text, which renders a LoopedActivity as its header only, so nothing inside a loop body was ever scope-checked
file: mdl/executor/cmd_alter_flow.go (applyTo outputChecks, noteRewritten, declSite/declaredAt, declaredOnPath, fragmentReads, checkFragmentScope, unscopedRefs, checkOutputUnused)
fix: Output-in-use checks are deferred until every operation is applied, and a return value or condition set in place marks its node rewritten (its stored reads retire, the new text's reads count). Each declared variable records the operation and stored target that put it in; declaredOnPath credits it to a later operation only when that site is upstream of where the later one goes (insert after / replace t: t strictly upstream; insert before t: also t itself, unless the later op is another insert before t) — used by both the fragment scope check and the condition check. fragmentReads walks loop bodies recursively, with the iterator and the body's own outputs local to the body
test: mdl/executor/cmd_alter_flow_scope_pedapp_test.go TestAlterMicroflow_ScopeRenameAcrossTheBlock, TestAlterMicroflow_ScopeDeclaredByAnEarlierOperation, TestAlterMicroflow_ScopeReplaceLoopChecksTheBody — each asserts check (CheckFlowVerdicts) and exec agree, with controls (a reader the block leaves, a declaration downstream, two inserts after one node, a body using its iterator and own declare). Revert controls: A2 stub (checks run inline) -> rename refused "$Code is still used by"; B2 stub -> "$Late … not declared on the path" (and the rename test fails on $Code2); B3 stub -> exec accepts $Nope. mx check: B3 script old binary 'Altered' + CE0109 (1 error) on 11.6.6 and 11.15.0, fixed binary refuses, nothing written, 0 errors; the rename + late-declare script on the fixed binary: 0 errors on both versions
insight: A block of patch operations aimed at the stored flow still writes one flow, so every verdict about variables has to be taken against that final flow — per-operation checks are order-dependent and refuse consistent edits. The A2 repro also hit B2 (the reader replacement reads the new $Code2 that op 1 declared), so one bug masked the other. And a scope check that scans rendered text inherits the renderer's elisions: formatActivity prints a loop as its header, so the body was invisible to every check built on it
